source_acquisition.search_note: The official adobe-research/EditVerse repository title exactly matches the paper and its README provides EditVerseBench/evaluation code, but its recursive tree has no plot, figure, table, LaTeX, notebook, SVG, or data-generation source. The local corpus/visual_sources/iclr-2026-df99a0fdd618 directory is absent. gh and unicli scholar found only the official evaluation repository plus paper-list/metadata mirrors; those mirrors are not visual sources. All visual properties below therefore use the 22-page PDF as the inventory fact source and 200 dpi rendered/PDF-object inspection.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Local semantic palettes: blue/peach/green token colors in architecture diagrams; orange/blue modality bands and blue/pink/purple instruction tags in qualitative collages; peach/gray win-tie-lose bars; red failure callouts; blue/red efficiency series; mostly grayscale booktabs tables with occasional gray EditVerse row highlight. Labels and position often provide redundancy, but there is no global color legend.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figure 2 and Figure 10 are predominantly vector; Figures 1, 3–9 combine embedded raster thumbnails/video frames with vector labels or borders; all tables are primarily PDF text/rules. The official repository contains no editable plot, table, or diagram source.
paper_style.style_consistency: Two-column Letter layout, numbered captions, Nimbus/Times-like body text and Computer Modern mathematics are stable. Figure 2/3 imported sans-serif text, raster montage typography, and Figure 10 chart labels form local substyles. Booktabs/minimal horizontal rules are consistent across tables, while density, gray row highlights, and caption completeness vary.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: The strong video editing performance of EditVerse emerges from a unified framework trained on a diverse set of mixed image and video data. This teaser visualizes a selection of supported image and video editing tasks (Instructions in the Appendix). More results in our Project Page.

color.semantic_mapping: Orange bands/tags identify video-editing examples and blue bands/tags identify image/conditional-editing examples; black/white labels add structural redundancy.

encodings.x: None; spatial left-to-right reading is not a quantitative axis.
encodings.y: None; upper/lower semantic bands separate video and image tasks.
encodings.color: Orange/blue section and task-tag colors encode modality and task family.
encodings.shape: Rounded cards, filmstrips and single-frame thumbnails encode example format.
encodings.line: Borders and separators encode cell/section boundaries.
encodings.facet: Video Editing versus Image Editing semantic bands.
encodings.text: Direct task labels encode supported operations such as Add/Remove/Change Object and Pose-to-Video.

figures.data_and_statistics: A selected qualitative collection of multimodal editing/generation examples (roughly 20+ cells) from the paper/project examples. It is not a coverage or performance estimate: no denominator, sampling rule, metric, or uncertainty is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: The unified mixed image/video training claim is introduced by the teaser; Figure 2/3 explain its architecture and interleaved token interface, while Figure 4 and Tables 1–2 quantify task/benchmark coverage and results.
design_strengths: Page-width first-page anchor makes the multimodal thesis immediately legible.
Direct task tags and filmstrip structure make many supported operations scannable.
Separate video/image bands provide a simple redundant modality cue.
design_weaknesses: Dense small thumbnails and unequal aspect ratios make local comparisons difficult.
The collage is a selection with no sampling protocol or quantitative success denominator.
Pastel color semantics weaken in grayscale and the caption cannot recover all task labels.
figures.reusable_pattern: Split a multimodal capability montage into labeled semantic bands, then connect the selection to a benchmark and appendix instructions.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Overview of EditVerse. We design a unified framework for image and video editing and generation, which processes text and vision inputs into a unified sequence. The right part of the figure shows our positional embedding design. This framework leverages full self-attention to facilitate robust in-context learning and effective knowledge transfer among modalities.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue marks Text T5 tokens, peach marks clean/noisy image/video VAE tokens, green marks start/end vision tokens, and gray/black carries attention and arrows.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: above/upper-left token stream and right inset

encodings.x: None; arrows provide process order from projected inputs to predicted velocity.
encodings.y: None; token lanes and right-side positional inset encode hierarchy.
encodings.color: Blue/peach/green token colors encode token type.
encodings.shape: Token blocks and rounded module boxes encode representation and processing stages.
encodings.line: Arrows encode flow; full-attention block boundary encodes the unified transformer.
encodings.facet: Main token pipeline and right positional-embedding inset.
encodings.text: Module names, N × 3D Full Attention Blocks, Predicted Velocity, and legend labels provide direct annotation.

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual architecture diagram; no sample count, benchmark value, parameter dimension beyond N × 3D, or uncertainty is plotted.
figures.evidence_relation: The method claim about unified text/vision processing leads to Figure 2; Figure 3 instantiates the interleaving pattern and Table 5 ablates interleave formation and sequential RoPE.
design_strengths: Architecture, token legend, and RoPE inset share one page-width reading path.
Color plus token labels/shapes provides partial redundancy.
The output velocity and full-attention block make the interface boundary explicit.
design_weaknesses: Many token segments and the right inset are small at two-column reading scale.
Concrete tensor shapes, masks, quantization placement, and computational cost are omitted.
Token colors are not fully grayscale-safe and the caption leaves details to the method text.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a token legend, a central unified block, and a right-side positional-encoding inset to connect model interface to mechanism.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Examples for the interleaved text and vision pattern. EditVerse is capable of processing image and video inputs and outputs of arbitrary resolution, duration, and sequential positions.

color.semantic_mapping: The Figure 2 blue/peach/green token palette is reused for text, vision, and start/end markers; position, token shape, and labels are redundant cues.

encodings.x: Spatial sequence order from user/input/output examples through concatenated tokens.
encodings.y: None; vertical placement separates chat examples, token stream, and More Examples.
encodings.color: Shared token palette encodes text/vision sequence elements.
encodings.shape: Chat cards, token blocks, dashed example frame, and thumbnails encode interaction/output roles.
encodings.line: Arrows and sequence connectors encode interleaving/order.
encodings.facet: Chat-like example, concatenated token stream, and More Examples panel.
encodings.text: Input instructions, token labels, and example operation labels directly identify the cases.

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual examples of image/video inputs and outputs; no measured resolution/duration range, sample denominator, performance value, or uncertainty is given. “Arbitrary” is a capability statement, not a plotted measurement.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 2 defines the unified token architecture; Figure 3 makes its interleaving user-facing, leading to §3.1–3.3 interfaces and Figure 4 benchmark/task coverage.
design_strengths: Concrete thumbnails connect the abstract token stream to user interaction.
Reuses Figure 2 token colors, preserving local semantic continuity.
Three regions give a short input-to-representation-to-output reading path.
design_weaknesses: More Examples thumbnails and labels are tiny.
Selected examples do not operationalize arbitrary resolution, duration, or position.
No temporal/shape dimensions or reproducible sampling protocol is visible.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4: Examples from the proposed EditVerseBench. EditVerseBench includes 200 editing pairs, evenly distributed across 20 editing categories as well as horizontal and vertical orientations.

color.semantic_mapping: Category headers and grid position identify the 20 task classes; blue/pink/purple inline tags encode video/image instruction slots, with borders and text supplying redundancy.

encodings.x: None; columns are qualitative category slots.
encodings.y: None; rows organize categories and orientation examples.
encodings.color: Inline blue/pink/purple tags encode <v1>/<v2>/<i1> slots; cell background/border encode grid.
encodings.shape: Thumbnail/filmstrip versus single frame indicates example format.
encodings.line: Cell borders provide grouping, not a quantitative line.
encodings.facet: Twenty task-category cells; some cells span multiple grid slots.
encodings.text: Category headings and instruction strings are direct labels.

figures.data_and_statistics: The benchmark contains 200 editing pairs evenly distributed across 20 categories and horizontal/vertical orientations; the paper describes 100 Pixabay videos (50 per orientation) and two prompts per video. The grid shows selected exemplars, not per-category performance or uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: The data pipeline and Table 1 motivate the benchmark; Figure 4 defines task coverage for Table 2/3 metrics, Figure 5 user study, and the selected prompts in Figures 6–8.
design_strengths: Broad task taxonomy, orientation coverage, and instruction context are visible at once.
A repeated cell schema supports cross-category scanning.
Direct category labels do not require a separate legend.
design_weaknesses: Twenty cells create very small text and unequal cell widths.
The meaning of <v1>/<v2>/<i1> tags is not keyed in the caption.
Exemplars show coverage but cannot establish quality or success rates.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a repeated category cell (header, input/output example, instruction) and state the pair/orientation denominator in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5: User study on EditVerseBench.

color.semantic_mapping: Stack segments encode win, tie, and lose preference proportions, respectively; legend, segment order, and direct percentage labels are redundant cues.

encodings.x: Normalized preference percentage (axis ticks are not visibly labeled).
encodings.y: Methods compared against EditVerse: Runway Aleph, Lucy Edit Dev, InsV2V, TokenFlow, STDF.
encodings.text: Method names and percentages are direct labels.

figures.data_and_statistics: The 100%-stacked bars show approximately Runway 51.7/26.3/22.0, Lucy 63.2/33.9/2.9, InsV2V 96.9 win, TokenFlow 97.0 win, and STDF 98.6 win. The study reports 3,000 pairwise ratings, 20 non-expert annotators, three annotators per pair and 150 pairs per annotator in the appendix; the plot has no denominator per bar or uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: Table 2 automatic metrics are checked against Figure 5 human preference; Figures 6–7 then provide matched qualitative context/edit-faithfulness examples.
design_strengths: 100% normalization makes preference composition comparable.
Direct labels preserve exact proportions despite tiny segments.
A compact single-column chart lists all comparison methods.
design_weaknesses: No visible x-axis ticks, denominator, tie definition, or agreement statistic.
Small tie/lose segments can disappear at page scale.
Method ordering and per-method effective pair count are not explained.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a 100% stacked preference bar with explicit win/tie/lose key and direct percentages; add effective ratings and uncertainty in the caption.

caption.text: Figure 6: Visualization of EditVerse and other video editing methods. EditVerse shows stronger context preservation and edit faithfulness. Complete comparisons are in the Appendix.

color.semantic_mapping: Method labels and frame positions identify conditions; red callouts mark Error Accumulation and Poor ID Preservation. Natural frame colors are content, not a quantitative palette.

encodings.x: None; frame order is a qualitative temporal snapshot.
encodings.y: None; method rows/panels encode comparison conditions.
encodings.color: Natural video-frame appearance plus red failure annotations.
encodings.shape: Frame strips and method panels encode source/method/result roles.
encodings.facet: Seven method/source panels under one hair-to-flames instruction.

figures.data_and_statistics: One hair-to-realistic-flames instruction is shown with roughly two frames for Source Video, TokenFlow, STDF, Señorita-2M, Runway Aleph, EditVerse/Ours, and InsV2V. No metric, denominator, temporal flicker analysis, or uncertainty is plotted.
figures.evidence_relation: Table 2 quantitative comparison is followed by this matched visual case; the appendix provides broader benchmark tables, while Figure 7 isolates Original/GT/Ours and Figure 9 shows failures.
design_strengths: Fixed instruction and frame positions make context preservation visually comparable.
Failure callouts direct attention to concrete qualitative weaknesses.
Ours is included in the same strip as open and commercial baselines.

Two frames and one prompt cannot support a general temporal claim.
Small raster frames and absent metric anchors limit reproducibility.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Figure 7: Compare EditVerse generated results with ground truth. Results show EditVerse can surpass ground-truth data quality by extracting knowledge from image and video generation data.

color.semantic_mapping: Original/ground-truth/Ours column labels and two prompt rows provide the encoding; frame colors are natural content and not a data series.

encodings.x: None; columns are Original Video, Ground Truth, and EditVerse (Ours).
encodings.color: Natural frame color; the second row intentionally shows black-and-white painting.
encodings.shape: Three-role frame strips encode source, target, and generated result.
encodings.line: Frame/grid boundaries encode task and role cells.
encodings.text: Prompt and column labels directly identify task/role.

figures.data_and_statistics: Two selected tasks are shown with two frames per Original/GT/Ours column: squirrel-to-small-mouse and black-and-white painting. There is no sample rate, metric, temporal evaluation, or uncertainty; “surpass” is a qualitative visual claim here.
figures.evidence_relation: Automatic metrics in Tables 2–3 lead to the matched ground-truth comparison; Figure 8/Table 4 then test whether image/video generation data explains this transfer.
design_strengths: Original/GT/Ours columns create a clear matched counterfactual structure.
Prompts are written above each row, keeping the task visible.
The visual supports the proposed generation-data transfer mechanism.
design_weaknesses: Only two examples are shown.
Quality is not operationalized by a metric or rating in the object.
Frame snapshots do not establish general temporal behavior.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use fixed Original/ground-truth/generated columns for mechanism examples, and pair them with a quantitative quality definition and sample protocol.

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Figure 8: Visualization of ablation on training data. Image data plays a critical role.

color.semantic_mapping: Column labels encode Original, w/o Image Data, w/o Video Gen Data, and Full Data; natural frame colors are content rather than a quantitative palette.

encodings.x: None; four columns encode training-data conditions.
encodings.y: None; two rows encode the crown and strawberry-to-dragon instructions.
encodings.color: Natural frame appearance; no color variable encodes score.
encodings.text: Prompt and condition labels are direct encodings.

figures.data_and_statistics: Two qualitative ablations compare Original Video, w/o Image Data, w/o Video Gen Data, and Full Data. The paper states image data is critical and both image/video generation data matter, but the figure has no seed, metric, sample count, data-volume matching, or uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: The mixed training recipe in Table 1 motivates Figure 8; Table 4 gives the corresponding 20K-step quantitative factor combinations and Table 5 tests model-design factors.
design_strengths: Four fixed columns make removal/completion conditions directly comparable.
Two task prompts expose both object addition and replacement behavior.
The qualitative panel is followed immediately by a numeric ablation table.
design_weaknesses: Qualitative evidence alone cannot separate data presence from volume/composition effects.
No replicate, seed, or metric is shown.
Tiny condition labels are difficult to read at two-column scale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Place original, single-source removals, and full-data outputs in fixed columns, then follow with a factor table using matched budgets.

color.semantic_mapping: Red text/circle marks the failure locus (wrong position or blur); frame labels and before/after placement provide redundant structure.

encodings.y: None; two failure cases are vertically faceted.
encodings.color: Red annotations identify the error location; natural image colors are content.

encodings.facet: Wrong Position and Blurred Editing Area cases.

caption.text: Figure 10: GPU memory usage and inference latency as functions of token length.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue encodes memory/20-step time and red encodes 50-step time; circle versus diamond markers redundantly identify step condition.

encodings.y: GPU Memory (GB) in the left panel; Inference Time (seconds) in the right panel.

design_strengths: Two resource dimensions share token length as a natural x variable.
Markers/legend separate 20-step and 50-step latency.
The adjacent table makes curve points auditable.

Latency growth is steep but axes are not log-scaled.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1: Statistics of the training datasets. We mix open-source datasets, internal datasets, and EditVerse datasets for unified training. Detailed information in Table 10.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty; counts are inventory values and filtered/pre-filtered quantities are mixed in the cells.
tables.data_and_statistics: Two blocks (Image Datasets, Video Datasets) are split into Edit/Gen groups. Image editing totals 6.0M and image generation 1.87M; video blocks list the compact editing/generation sources. K/M values, parenthetical pre-filter volume, * before filtering, and † internal are used.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 3 dataset pipeline leads to the compact recipe in Table 1; Figure 8/Table 4 ablate its components and Table 10 expands counts/ratios.
design_strengths: Compact modality×task row groups fit the main column.
Totals provide a quick view of the mixed recipe.
Table 10 pointer preserves a detailed reproduction path.
design_weaknesses: K/M and pre-filter parentheses are easy to confuse.
Vertical/compact group labels and two-column width compress readability.
No quality, filtering-failure, ratio, or uncertainty field is included.
tables.reusable_pattern: Keep modality×task totals in the main paper and move dataset-level counts, ratios, and filtering details to a companion table.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2: Quantitative comparison on EditVerseBench. For open-source research models, we compare two training-free methods (TokenFlow and STDF), one first-frame propagation method (Señorita-2M), and one instruction-guided video editing method (InsV2V). Best results are highlighted in bold. We also provide the results of a commercial model, Runway Aleph. While EditVerse lags Runway Aleph in generation quality due to base model differences, our proposed method EditVerse surpasses it in editing faithfulness (via VLM evaluation on editing quality), aligning better with human judgment that is further validated by user studies shown in Figure 5.

tables.uncertainty: No error bars, intervals, significance markers, per-method denominator, or replicate summary.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six metrics: VLM editing quality, PickScore video quality, frame/video text alignment, and CLIP/DINO temporal consistency. EditVerse row is 7.65, 20.07, 26.73, 23.93, 98.56, 98.42; Runway is higher on some generation/temporal values. Values are point estimates to two decimals.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 4 defines the 200-pair benchmark; Table 2 is the main quantitative comparison and is triangulated by Figure 5 human preference and Figure 6 visual comparison.
design_strengths: Two-level metric-family header separates faithfulness, quality, alignment, and temporal consistency.
Method-paradigm row groups expose heterogeneous baselines.
Caption explains the commercial-model/base-model boundary and Figure 5 link.
design_weaknesses: Mixed metric scales make cross-column visual comparison unsafe.
No uncertainty, cost, sample count, or evaluation repetition is shown.
Bold best values can overstate tiny point-estimate differences.
tables.reusable_pattern: Combine method-paradigm groups with a multi-level metric header and explicitly state commercial-baseline and metric boundaries in the caption.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3: Quantitative comparison on TGVE+. Results show superior performance of EditVerse.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, benchmark denominator, or repeated-run summary.
tables.data_and_statistics: Nine methods are compared on ViCLIPdir and ViCLIPout; EditVerse is approximately .225/.252. Values are point estimates to three decimals.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 2 main benchmark results lead to the narrower TGVE+ extension; Figure 7 and Appendix Table 9 broaden qualitative and V2V comparisons.
design_strengths: Compact width makes the two directional metrics easy to scan.
Consistent three-decimal precision supports small metric differences.
Best-value emphasis identifies the intended comparison quickly.
design_weaknesses: Caption says superior without defining metrics or sample scope.
No uncertainty or cross-benchmark protocol details are visible.
Narrow table depends on正文 for metric semantics.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a small directional-metric table after the main benchmark, with metric definitions and evaluation protocol in the caption or adjacent text.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4: Ablation study on training data. We run 20K steps with the same setup as in Section 5.1. Results indicate that both image and video generation data are crucial to video editing performance.

tables.uncertainty: No replicate, variance, uncertainty, or data-volume-matched comparison is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: Three binary training-data columns (Image, Video Gen, Video Edit) are paired with six Table-2-aligned metrics. The full ✓✓✓ row is bold and is approximately 6.95, 19.99, 26.26, 23.81, 98.68, 98.44.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 8 gives qualitative removal examples; Table 4 quantifies the five combinations at 20K steps, linking back to Table 2 and forward to Table 5 design ablation.
design_strengths: Explicit factor flags make the mechanism question legible.
Shared metrics allow direct comparison to the main table.
Caption fixes the reduced 20K-step training setting.
design_weaknesses: Modality presence and total data volume/composition change together.
No uncertainty or replicate information limits causal strength.
Missing cost/ratio columns make resource trade-offs opaque.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use binary factor columns and a shared metric vector for data ablations, while matching or reporting token budget and cost.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5: Ablation study on interleaved formation and sequential RoPE. We run 20K steps with the same experimental setting detailed in Section 5.1 for the ablation to save compute.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, replicate, full-training comparison, or computational cost is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: Two design flags (Interleave, Sequential PE) and six outcome metrics are reported for ✓✓, ✗✓, and ✓✗. The full design is approximately 6.95, 19.99, 26.26, 23.81, 98.68, 98.44.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 2 introduces the architecture/RoPE design; Table 5 tests its two toggles after Table 4 data ablation and supports the interleaved-sequence mechanism.
design_strengths: Isolates two interface/positional factors using familiar metrics.
Full design is highlighted and aligned with the main result vector.
Caption discloses the compute-saving 20K-step setting.
design_weaknesses: Sequential PE abbreviation is not expanded in the caption.
Reduced training steps may not reflect the final recipe.
Small point differences have no uncertainty or cost context.
tables.reusable_pattern: Represent architecture choices as explicit binary toggles and reuse the main metric vector, with a clear training-budget caveat.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6: Quantitative comparison on ImgEdit-Bench (Ye et al., 2025a).

tables.uncertainty: No task-level denominator, repeated-run statistic, uncertainty, or cost.
tables.data_and_statistics: Thirteen image-editing methods are evaluated over Add, Adjust, Extract, Replace, Remove, Background, Style, Hybrid, Action, and Overall. EditVerse row is gray-highlighted and Overall is about 3.42; values are point estimates to two decimals.
tables.evidence_relation: Extends the main video editing evidence to ImgEdit-Bench and makes the image-domain boundary visible alongside Table 8 generation results.
design_strengths: Task columns expose where image editing succeeds or lags.
Overall column provides a compact summary.
Gray row makes the paper method easy to locate in a dense appendix table.
design_weaknesses: Very small font across eleven columns.
Caption does not define task scores or gray-row meaning.
Cross-model settings and uncertainty are not visible.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use task-level columns plus Overall for image-editing extensions, with benchmark score definitions and row-highlight key in the caption.

tables.label: Table 7

caption.text: Table 7: Comparison with text-to-video models on the VBench (Zhang et al., 2024). # Params. is the number of total parameters. EditVerse shows competitive performance with a small model size.

tables.uncertainty: No sample denominator, hardware, repeated-run or uncertainty information.
tables.data_and_statistics: Thirteen text-to-video models show parameter count, Total, Quality Score, and Semantic Score. EditVerse is 2B with 80.97 total, 83.47 quality, and 70.97 semantic; its gray row supports the small-model-competitive claim.
tables.evidence_relation: Adds text-to-video generation evidence to the unified model story; Figure 10/Table 11 then expose the token-length resource cost. It is not a replacement for video-editing Table 2.
design_strengths: Parameters and multiple VBench scores make the size/performance trade-off explicit.
Compact row structure supports baseline scanning.
Caption defines # Params. and states the intended comparison.
design_weaknesses: Single-column density makes labels and gray highlight small.
No cost/quality uncertainty or sampling protocol.
The gray-row encoding is not explicitly explained in the caption.
tables.reusable_pattern: Report model size beside quality/semantic scores for generation extensions, with explicit evaluation conditions.

tables.label: Table 8

caption.text: Table 8: Comparison with text-to-image models on the GenEval (Zhang et al., 2024).

tables.uncertainty: No prompt count, repeated-run statistic, uncertainty, or score denominator.
tables.data_and_statistics: Thirteen text-to-image methods are compared on Single Obj., Two Obj., Counting, Colors, Position, Color Attri., and Overall. EditVerse is approximately .99/.95/.81/.82/.68/.64/.82, with a gray row; † methods use LLM-rewritten prompts per the surrounding text.
tables.evidence_relation: Connects the unified image/video interface to image-generation capability; Table 6 shows image-editing limits and Figure 7 uses generation data as a qualitative mechanism example.
design_strengths: Compositional task breakdown prevents Overall-only reporting.
Overall remains visible for quick cross-method comparison.
Wide layout allows seven task metrics without nesting.
design_weaknesses: Caption omits task key, dagger prompt caveat, and gray-row meaning.
Small font and no uncertainty weaken fine-grained comparisons.
Generation score does not directly establish image-editing SOTA.
tables.reusable_pattern: Preserve compositional task columns and Overall, while making prompt transformations and denominator explicit.

tables.label: Table 9

caption.text: Table 9: Quantitative comparison on V2VBench (Sun et al., 2024). Methods are grouped into three categories: (i) Network and Training Paradigm, (ii) Attention Feature Injection, and (iii) Diffusion Latent Manipulation. Local best are in bold. Global best are underlined.

tables.uncertainty: No error/uncertainty, benchmark denominator, repeated runs, or per-group cost.
tables.data_and_statistics: Seventeen methods are grouped into three intervention paradigms and compared on Frames Quality, Semantic/Object Consistency, Frames Text Alignment, Frames Pick Score, Video Text Alignment, and Motion Alignment. Values are mostly three-decimal point estimates; local best is bold and global best underlined.
tables.evidence_relation: Extends Table 2 beyond EditVerseBench to V2VBench and method paradigms; Figure 6 qualitative context/failure examples provide a visual companion.
design_strengths: Paradigm row groups make intervention assumptions visible.
Local/global best encodings are defined in the caption.
Metric family spans visual quality, consistency, alignment, and motion.
design_weaknesses: Seventeen rows and eight columns are very dense.
No variance, sample count, or cost makes small differences hard to interpret.
Cross-paradigm protocol comparability depends on正文.
tables.reusable_pattern: Group external methods by intervention paradigm, distinguish local/global best, and report group-specific evaluation constraints.

tables.label: Table 10

caption.text: Table 10: Detailed Statistics of the training datasets. We combine high-quality open-source datasets, internal datasets, and EditVerse datasets for unified training. This table presents the dataset name, sample counts, training ratios, and key details for each dataset.

tables.uncertainty: No quality distribution, filtering-failure counts, seed, or uncertainty; counts/ratios are recipe metadata.
tables.data_and_statistics: Four columns (Dataset, #Samples, #Ratio, Information) cover Image Editing, Image Generation, Video Editing, and Video Generation groups with Sum rows. Counts and ratios use mixed K/M/text precision. Visible text includes typos such as High-quaity, Object Chnage, and Generated wih.
tables.evidence_relation: Expands Table 1 totals into dataset-level denominator/ratio information, supporting Figure 3 and the data combinations in Figure 8/Table 4.
design_strengths: Dataset, count, ratio, and information are all present for reproduction.
Four modality/task groups mirror the main data story.
Sum rows provide a reconciliation target for Table 1.
design_weaknesses: Long table and small font reduce scanability.
Typos and mixed units undermine polish and exact reconciliation.
No quality/failure field connects sample count to training value.
tables.reusable_pattern: Keep dataset provenance in a four-column appendix table with normalized units, filtering stage, and quality/coverage fields.

tables.label: Table 11

caption.text: Table 11: Inference efficiency across different token lengths

tables.uncertainty: No hardware, batch, warm-up, replicate, or uncertainty field.
tables.data_and_statistics: Four rows report Inference Time (20 steps), Inference Time (50 steps), GPU Memory (MB), and TFLOPs/second across token lengths 17,652, 34,342, 63,662, and 110,822. Values are exact point readings corresponding to Figure 10.
tables.evidence_relation: Provides exact values for the two Figure 10 curves and the appendix resource/cost limitation; it does not independently establish general throughput.
design_strengths: Exact values make the adjacent curves auditable.
Four token-length columns make the scaling direction immediate.
Compact inset avoids duplicating a full plot.
design_weaknesses: Long token-length headers and mixed units are dense.
Measurement environment and repetition are absent.
Caption alone cannot reproduce the values or explain TFLOPs calculation.
tables.reusable_pattern: Pair trend curves with a compact exact-value table and include measurement environment in the caption.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 presents the unified image/video thesis; Figures 2–3 define the full-attention/interleaved token interface; Figure 4 and Table 1 define benchmark/data coverage; Table 2–3 and Figures 5–7 triangulate automatic metrics, human preference, and matched qualitative cases; Figure 8 and Tables 4–5 test data/design mechanisms; Appendix Tables 6–10 extend modality and data detail, while Figure 9 and Figure 10/Table 11 disclose failure and resource boundaries.
cross_object_system.caption_system: All 10 Figures and 11 Tables have numbered captions below the object. Table 2, Table 4, and Table 9 carry the richest comparison/setup/highlight information. Figure 5, Figure 10, Table 3, Table 6, Table 8, and Table 11 are title-only or short captions, leaving denominator, hardware, metric keys, or main findings to正文; qualitative captions do not state sample-selection protocols.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables 2, 4, and 5 use two-level metric/factor headers; Tables 3, 7, and 11 use compact one-level headers; Tables 6, 8, and 9 expand external benchmark metrics; Tables 1 and 10 use modality/task dataset groups. Horizontal booktabs/minimal rules and no vertical rules dominate, with bold/underline/gray row highlights as local encodings.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figures 2–3 establish architecture and interleaving, Table 1/Table 10 establish the mixed training recipe, Table 2/Table 3 and Figures 5–7 establish video-editing results, Figure 8/Table 4 test training-data factors, and Table 5 tests interleave/RoPE. The mechanism-to-result-to-ablation chain is coherent but mostly point-estimate based.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figure 4 and Table 2 link to Appendix Tables 6/9; main Table 1 links to Table 10; Figures 2–3 link to Table 5 and Figure 8; Figure 6 points to complete appendix comparisons; Appendix Figures 9–10/Table 11 turn positive capability claims into explicit failure and cost boundaries.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Page text/captions consistently use NimbusRomanNo9L/Times-like and Computer Modern math. Imported Arial/Aptos or raster text in diagrams and qualitative strips creates local variation; Table 6/8/9/10 small body sizes are the main cross-object readability constraint.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: The blue/peach/green token palette is reused between Figures 2–3. Other objects use local modality, task-tag, preference, failure, or efficiency colors; tables are mostly grayscale with a gray EditVerse row. Labels/position generally duplicate color semantics, but grayscale and cross-figure color portability are not guaranteed.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 1 multimodal task bands with direct tags provide a compact headline capability map.
Figures 2–3 combine a token legend, unified block, positional inset, and concrete interleaving examples.
Figure 4 repeats a benchmark cell schema to show category/orientation coverage and instruction slots.
Table 2 combines method-paradigm row groups with a multi-level metric-family header, then connects to human and qualitative evidence.
Figure 8 plus Tables 4–5 turn qualitative factor removal into numeric data/design ablations; Figure 10 plus Table 11 pair trend curves with exact values.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 anchors the unified image/video thesis and supported-task breadth.
Figures 2–3 are the core method-interface and mechanism visuals.
Table 2 is the main EditVerseBench quantitative comparison.
Figure 5, Figure 7, and Figure 8/Table 4 triangulate human preference, generation-data transfer, and data necessity.
failure_patterns: Qualitative Figures 5–9 rely on selected examples or normalized summaries without consistent denominators, repeats, or uncertainty.
Tables 2–3 and 6–9 report cross-model point estimates without variance, cost, or protocol detail.
Figures 4, 6, 8 and Tables 6, 9, 10 use dense small text that degrades at two-column scale.
Short captions (especially Figure 5/10 and Tables 3/6/8/11) make objects hard to audit outside正文.
Table 10 contains visible spelling/typographic errors and mixed count/ratio units; Figure 10 lacks hardware and measurement repetition.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: EditVerse makes a unified interleaved multimodal token/attention architecture the visual spine, establishes broad mixed-data and benchmark coverage, triangulates results with metrics, users, and matched examples, ablates data/design factors, and discloses failure and token-length cost boundaries in the appendix.
